name: std::ranges::greater
intro: Function object for performing comparisons. Deduces the parameter types of the function call operator from the arguments (but not the return type).

sections.title: Member functions
sections.text:
operator()

  checks if the first argument is greater than the second 
 (public member function)

std::ranges::greater::operator()



 template< class T, class U >

constexpr bool operator()( T&& t, U&& u ) const;
  
  



Equivalent to return ranges::less{}(std::forward<U>(u), std::forward<T>(t));.
This overload participates in overload resolution only if std::totally_ordered_with<T, U> is satisfied.

sections.title: Notes
sections.text:
Unlike std::greater, std::ranges::greater requires all six comparison operators <, <=, >, >=, == and != to be valid (via the  totally_ordered_with constraint) and is entirely defined in terms of 
std::ranges::less.
